les: Handel wat ook vir die boer werk
kaps_punt: Regverdige handel - Gevallestudies van 'n positiewe projek

items.bewering: Baie Suid-Afrikaanse huise het 'n boks rooibostee in die kombuis.
items.bron: SA Rooibos Council, citing an Insight Survey of more than 25 000 adults: the share of South Africans who drink rooibos rose from 29.4% (2011) to 30.9% (2015) (citizen.co.za, 21 Jul 2016, 'Latest tea consumption figures tip scale in favour of rooibos'; repeated in georgeherald.com, 11 Jul 2017). sarooibos.co.za, 'Heritage Month Survey Reveals How South Africans Enjoy Rooibos the Most'. Roughly a third of adults drinking it is enough to support 'baie huise'. The figures are 2015-2019 and the council is an advocacy body, but the claim is vague enough that this supports it.

items.bewering: Die plant groei op die Suid Bokkeveld-plato naby Nieuwoudtville in die Noord-Kaap.
items.bron: Taken alone, the sentence is true. Hawkins, Malgas & Bienabe 2011, S Afr J Bot (UP repository, 'Ecotypes of wild rooibos ... are ecologically distinct'): rooibos 'is cultivated by small- and large-scale commercial farmers of the Cederberg and Bokkeveld Plateau'. Trade Aid NZ's partner page and EMG put Heiveld's farmers in the Suid Bokkeveld, Northern Cape, with an EMG field office in Nieuwoudtville. The fault is the picture the sentence gives. It comes straight after the box of rooibos in 'baie Suid-Afrikaanse huise' and calls rooibos 'Die plant', so a learner will read the Suid Bokkeveld as where rooibos grows: the source of the tea in their own kitchen. SANBI (PlantZAfrica, via search) says rooibos tea is made from forms of the species found 'mainly on the Cederberg Mountains', which is in the Western Cape. The species grows naturally from about Vanrhynsdorp southwards. The Nature-based Solutions Initiative case study and the UCT 2025 article both say most rooibos is grown by large commercial farms elsewhere in the rooibos area. The Suid Bokkeveld is real rooibos country but only one part of a wider area.
items.regstelling: Say that rooibos grows only in a small area in the west of the country, mainly in the Cederberg in the Western Cape. Then say that the Suid Bokkeveld plateau near Nieuwoudtville in the Northern Cape is one of the places where it grows, and that this lesson's farmers live there. Do not let the sentence read as if it names the only place, or the main place, where rooibos grows.

items.bewering: Boere daar plant rooibos in lande en oes ook rooibos wat wild op die veld groei.
items.bron: Hawkins et al. 2011, S Afr J Bot: rooibos is cultivated on the Bokkeveld Plateau, and 'Small-scale farmers also harvest A. linearis from the wild'. UCT OpenUCT thesis 'Sustainable harvesting of wild rooibos (Aspalathus linearis) in the Suid Bokkeveld, Northern Cape' (Louw 2006) was requested by Heiveld for its members as managers of wild stands. CEPF final project report 1342/1483 covers wild rooibos harvesting under Heiveld's guidelines. The Citizen (24 Oct 2022, 'Small-scale organic rooibos farmers become climate smart'): Nieuwoudtville-area farmers grow rooibos on plots from 5x5 m to 50 ha.

items.bewering: In 2001 het 'n groep van hierdie boere die Heiveld-koöperasie gestig.
items.bron: stories.coop, 'Rooibos farmers join together...' (seen via search; the page now returns 404): 'founded by 14 members in early January 2001'. A German-language Heiveld producer profile (hubbs.schule, via search): 'Im Januar 2001 haben sich 14 Frauen und Männer zusammengeschlossen und die Heiveld Kooperative gegründet'. UWC master's thesis on Heiveld (etd.uwc.ac.za 11394/2664, via search): 'Established in 2001'. A 2001 99-year land lease 'to the newly-created Heiveld cooperative' agrees. One outlier, agro.biodiver.se (7 Mar 2010), says 'established in 2003' while citing UKaid funding. It is a single aggregator post and is probably dating a funding round, so 2001 is clearly the better-supported date. The claim says only 'n groep, which avoids the founder count.

items.bewering: 'n Boer met 'n klein oes tee staan swak wanneer hy alleen verkoop. Hy het dikwels net een koper naby genoeg om sy tee te koop.
items.blok: Waarom 'n klein boer alleen swak staan
items.bron: For these farmers specifically: EMG describes Suid-Bokkeveld rooibos farmers as marginalised by apartheid and 'the monopoly rooibos processing industry' (emg.org.za, small-scale farmers page, via search). stories.coop (via search) says they 'were dependent on processing facilities owned by larger farmers'. The Nature-based Solutions Initiative case study (via search) describes larger farmers acting as middlemen and setting unfairly low prices. In general: smallholder-marketing research lists 'absence of competitive buyers' and weak bargaining power as core constraints (Ethiopian banana value-chain study; Nyikahadzoi et al., AJARD 3(5) 2013, ageconsearch.umn.edu).

items.bewering: Hy weet ook nie wat sy tee verder langs die ketting haal nie. So 'n boer het min keuse en min inligting, en hy neem die prys wat hy kry. Daarom kry hy dikwels minder vir sy tee as wat dit werd is.
items.blok: Waarom 'n klein boer alleen swak staan
items.bron: The Determinants of price received by cocoa farmers in Cameroon study (agris.fao.org) finds that where prices are non-negotiable and information favours traders, 'the traders seize the entire surplus'. Smallholder studies name price-information asymmetry as a constraint. FAO (sfcs.fao.org, 'More market power for Kenya's farmers') reports that farmers selling as a group gain negotiating power and 'a clear idea of their produce's price'. The 2011 Raynolds report on emerging rooibos farmers (UC Davis, executive summary) says inequitable functioning of the rooibos commodity network kept them from developing market-access skills and resources. 'Dikwels' keeps this a general tendency rather than a universal rule, which is how the sources state it.

items.bewering: verder langs die ketting (the supply chain pictured as a chain)
items.blok: Waarom 'n klein boer alleen swak staan
items.bron: The mapping holds. The tea passes in order from farmer to processor to trader to shop, as in a value or supply chain, and the price rises at each link. 'Value chain' is the standard term in the smallholder-marketing literature cited above, and the Raynolds report speaks of the rooibos 'commodity network'. A learner who reasons further from the image (each link adds something, and someone further along gets more) reaches a correct conclusion. This is the only comparison in the lesson. The lesson has no other analogies.

items.bewering: In 'n koöperasie werk die boere saam en besit hulle die besigheid self.
items.bron: ICA Statement on the Cooperative Identity (1995), quoted in the Western Cape Government's 'Principles of a cooperative' (westerncape.gov.za, 2004): a co-operative is 'an autonomous association of persons united voluntarily ... through a jointly-owned and democratically-controlled enterprise'. FAO agroecology database: Heiveld 'is a member-owned business'.

items.bewering: Heiveld se boere bring hul tee bymekaar en verkoop dit as een.
items.bron: FAO agroecology database (via search): Heiveld 'processes and markets organic and fair-trade certified rooibos tea produced by its members', and its primary business is to market members' tea to trading companies. stories.coop (via search): by 2005 Heiveld had its own tea court where members' rooibos is chopped, fermented and dried. The Citizen (2022): rooibos is dried on the tea court at Blomfontein 'and then packed into 50kg bales for export'.

items.bewering: Die koöperasie voer die tee uit op voorwaardes van regverdige handel.
items.bron: FAO agroecology database: Heiveld markets 'organic and fair-trade certified rooibos tea ... to trading companies, most of which are in the global north'. Witt FairTrade Tea Collection 2021 (via search): Heiveld 'exports the rooibos it produces organically and through Fairtrade'. Trade Aid NZ, a fair trade importer, lists Heiveld as a current partner (tradeaid.org.nz/partner/heiv/). Ponte/Raynolds-era research (Geoforum 2010) says Heiveld and Wupperthal's jointly owned Fairpackers facility exports shelf-ready tea. Caveat: I found no 2025-2026 certificate record. The present tense rests on the 2021 source and Trade Aid's live partner page.

items.bewering: Wie self aan die koper verkoop, weet ook self wat sy tee haal.
items.bron: The Nature-based Solutions Initiative case study (via search): with its certifications the coop 'is able to sell its product at a premium and directly on the market, bypassing middlemen'. FAO, 'More market power for Kenya's farmers': group sellers have 'a clear idea of their produce's price'. In context, 'self' means the cooperative selling to the buyer, not each farmer, and that reading is supported.

items.bewering: Saam het die boere meer keuse as wat elkeen alleen sou hê. Hulle kies saam aan watter kopers hulle hul tee verkoop.
items.blok: Wat dit vir die boere beteken
items.bron: stories.coop (via search): the prospect of a Dutch Fair Trade buyer (talks with the Fair Trade Organisatie, Nov 2000) helped prompt the coop, which then sold directly. FAO says Heiveld sells to several trading companies abroad. Witt 2021 and agro.biodiver.se list buyers in Europe, North America, Japan, New Zealand and South Africa. On collective choice: ICA principle 2, democratic member control (westerncape.gov.za principles sheet). Nyikahadzoi et al. 2013: collective action increases smallholders' bargaining power.

items.bewering: Regverdige handel vra dat die koper 'n regverdige prys vir hul werk betaal.
items.blok: Wat dit vir die boere beteken
items.bron: FLOCERT glossary, 'Fairtrade Minimum Price': 'the minimum price that must be paid by buyers to producers' for certification, set to cover production costs. Fairtrade International FAQ (fairtrade.net/about/faq): the minimum is a safety net, and the buyer pays the market price if it is higher, plus the Fairtrade Premium. WFTO/FINE definition (wfto-europe.org): a trading partnership offering 'better trading conditions' to marginalised producers. The lesson's simplified version is accurate.

items.bewering: Die boere besit die koöperasie self. Hulle neem daarom saam die groot besluite oor sy geld en sy werk.
items.blok: Wat dit vir die boere beteken
items.bron: FAO: Heiveld is 'a member-owned business'. stories.coop (via search), quoting EMG's Noel Oettle: Heiveld's constitution divides profits, 70% to members by the business each did with the coop and 30% equally among the less wealthy members, so members' own constitution decides the money. ICA definition: 'democratically-controlled enterprise' (westerncape.gov.za). SANBI document 'Heiveld Co-operative: a community driven sustainable rooibos industry' (CAPE Partners 2009): 'Each member of the co-operative makes an important contribution' and stresses 'ownership'.

items.bewering: Die tradisionele kennis van rooibos behoort aan die San en die Khoi-Khoi.
items.bron: gov.za, 'Minister Barbara Creecy launches rooibos access and benefit-sharing agreement, 1 Nov': a study concluded in 2015 'found that the San and Khoi-khoi hold the traditional knowledge for rooibos and honeybush'. Herald and Sowetan (Nov 2019) report Creecy calling them 'the rightful holders and owners of traditional knowledge associated with the use of Rooibos species'. DFFE Biodiversity Investment page (biodiversityinvestment.environment.gov.za/node/253) agrees. Nuance only, not a contradiction: UCT News (17 Sep 2025) notes that small-scale rooibos-growing communities were included only as 'rooibos indigenous farming communities' through the National Khoisan Council. The lesson's statement matches the official finding the agreement rests on.

items.bewering: In 2019 het die rooibos-bedryf ooreengekom om hulle gemeenskappe elke jaar vir daardie kennis te betaal.
items.bron: gov.za (Creecy, media advisory and speech): the agreement was signed 1 November 2019 at !Kwa Ttu, Yzerfontein, by the SA Rooibos Council, the National Khoi-San Council and the SA San Council. Business Report (1 Nov 2019, 'Landmark deal to give Khoi and San benefit-sharing levy in rooibos') and The Herald (2 Nov 2019): a levy of 1.5% of the farm gate price from 1 January 2019, paid annually. DFFE Biodiversity Investment: 'The processors will pay an annual levy of 1.5%'. UCT News (17 Sep 2025) still describes the levy as about US$700 000 'per year', so it is ongoing. 'Elke jaar' is accurate. The first year was called a pilot, with annual reviews.

items.bewering: Die verwerkers van rooibos betaal daarvoor 'n klein deel van die prys wat 'n boer by die plaashek kry.
items.bron: DFFE Biodiversity Investment (node/253): processors pay 'an annual levy of 1.5% based on the actual Rooibos purchased', calculated on the Farm Gate Price. Business Report / Herald, Nov 2019: 'benefit-sharing levy of 1.5% of the farm gate price', paid by processors; the farm gate price is 'the price paid by processors to the farmers who grow, harvest or ferment and dry rooibos'. 1.5% is fairly called 'n klein deel'. Note for the person, not a fault: UCT News (2025) reports that small-scale farmers are 'expected to pay towards the levy' because they produce rooibos, so part of the cost may be passed back to growers. Formally, the processors pay, which is what the lesson says.

items.bewering: Heiveld se plan kom van die boere self en is nie aan hulle gegee nie.
items.bron: SANBI, 'Heiveld Co-operative: a community driven sustainable rooibos industry' (CAPE Partners 2009): 'the Heiveld Cooperative is one which can truly claim to be driven by the community'. stories.coop (via search): 'After deciding to form a business organization, a group of rooibos farmers chose the cooperative structure', motivated by their dependence on larger farmers' processing facilities. Context the person should know: the farmers had outside support. EMG (an NGO) had worked with the community since 1998, there were talks with the Dutch Fair Trade Organisatie in Nov 2000, and a German profile mentions Canadian start-up aid for equipment. The UWC thesis calls the founding the 'culmination of long years of exploration and collaboration between local producers, Rooibos traders, and other consultants'. The sentence is still true: the decision and the plan were the farmers', and support is not the same as being handed a plan. If the lesson ever says the farmers did it with no help, that would be false.

items.bewering: Die koöperasie help die boere wat daarin is.
items.bron: FAO agroecology database: Heiveld provides 'a number of supplementary services to its members including training in organic and sustainable production, provision of organic farming inputs, and an internal organic control system'. EMG (via search): fair trade and organic market access mean that 'tea-growing is no longer merely a survival strategy, but a viable farming activity'. agro.biodiver.se (2010): fair trade 'has tripled the farmers' income'.

items.bewering: Onregverdige handel elders in die wêreld is daarmee nie opgelos nie.
items.bron: Even inside rooibos, UCT News (17 Sep 2025, 'SA's small-scale rooibos tea growers not benefitting enough') reports that the white-dominated industry still owns most tea lands and cultivates about 93% of rooibos. The Nature-based Solutions Initiative case study (via search) says only about 2% of Bokkeveld land is owned by local small producers. The wider claim is a self-evident limit on one cooperative's reach.

items.bewering: Heiveld wys wel dat handel tussen Suid-Afrika en die wêreld meer regverdig kan word.
items.bron: This is an evaluative conclusion, and it is supported. EMG: higher prices on fair trade and organic markets made rooibos a viable business for Heiveld's members, who raised capital for their own processing facility. agro.biodiver.se (2010): fair trade tripled members' income. SANBI/CAPE 2009 presents Heiveld as a model community-driven enterprise. 'Kan ... meer regverdig' is appropriately modest.

items.bewering: koöperasie: 'n Besigheid wat sy eie lede saam besit en saam bestuur.
items.bron: ICA Statement on the Cooperative Identity (1995), via the westerncape.gov.za principles sheet: 'jointly-owned and democratically-controlled enterprise'. 'Saam besit en saam bestuur' maps onto 'jointly owned and democratically controlled' without falsifying it. Day-to-day management may be delegated to elected people or staff, but control stays with the members.

items.bewering: voorwaardes: Die dinge waarop 'n koper en 'n verkoper ooreenkom voor hulle handel.
items.bron: In this lesson's use ('op voorwaardes van regverdige handel'), the word means the terms of a trade. Fairtrade International uses the matching English phrase, 'products sold on Fairtrade terms' (fairtrade.net FAQ), meaning the agreed minimum price and premium. The Dutch cognate is glossed as 'term' / 'stipulation' and 'a statement of what is required as part of an agreement' (interglot.nl, vocabulary.com nl). I could not reach an Afrikaans dictionary entry (Viva or WAT) through search. The definition matches the cognate and the Fairtrade usage, and is narrowed correctly to the trading sense.

items.bewering: verwerker: Iemand wat 'n oes verder bewerk voordat dit in die winkel kom.
items.bron: Business Report / Herald, Nov 2019, and DFFE: rooibos 'processors' are the businesses that buy rooibos from farmers at the farm gate. DFFE: the levy applies to 'actual Rooibos purchased' by processors, who then prepare it for sale. stories.coop and The Citizen (2022) describe the processing steps: chopping, fermenting, drying, then packing for export or retail. The definition is accurate. 'Iemand' includes companies, which is acceptable at this level.

items.bewering: tradisionele kennis: Kennis wat 'n groep mense oor baie geslagte opgebou en oorgedra het.
items.bron: WIPO, Traditional Knowledge page (wipo.int/en/web/traditional-knowledge/tk): 'knowledge, know-how, skills and practices that are developed, sustained and passed on from generation to generation within a community'. The lesson's definition maps onto this closely.

opsomming: One claim is contradicted and nothing is uncertain: the first block places rooibos on the Suid Bokkeveld plateau right after the box in South African kitchens, so a learner will think rooibos comes from there, when most of it grows in the Cederberg in the Western Cape and the Suid Bokkeveld is one place it grows, where this lesson's farmers live. Every other claim checks out against at least two independent sources, including all the Heiveld details (founded 2001, wild and cultivated rooibos, member-owned, Fairtrade exports) and the 2019 San and Khoi-Khoi agreement (an annual 1.5% of the farm gate price, paid by processors). The lesson has no superlatives, and its one comparison (the chain) holds.
